background_boundary: Programming, linear algebra, elementary probability, and operating-system concepts are background; this draft does not attempt to enumerate those disciplines.

concepts.definition: Measurable desired behavior and constraints for a specified workload.
concepts.label: System requirements

concepts.definition: A reference method or system used to justify the value of a proposed change.
concepts.label: Baseline

concepts.definition: A measurable target used in place of the outcome actually desired.
concepts.label: Proxy objective

concepts.definition: A target for a defined service measure over a specified population and window.
concepts.label: Service-level objective

concepts.definition: The input, request, model, and execution distributions that a system must support.
concepts.label: Workload characterization

concepts.definition: The choice of where system components execute, such as device, edge, or datacenter.
concepts.label: Execution placement

concepts.definition: Fitness of recorded examples for the intended task, including validity, coverage, and error.
concepts.label: Data quality

concepts.definition: The correctness, consistency, and coverage of recorded supervision relative to the intended task, which bound the training signal and the trustworthiness of evaluation.
concepts.label: Label quality

concepts.definition: Constructing model inputs whose semantics and availability match the task.
concepts.label: Feature engineering

concepts.definition: Absent observations whose pattern and treatment can change learned behavior.
concepts.label: Missing data

concepts.definition: Information unavailable at the intended prediction boundary entering development or evaluation.
concepts.label: Data leakage

concepts.definition: Constructing examples using only information available at their stated prediction time.
concepts.label: Point-in-time correctness

concepts.definition: Recorded dependencies that identify the sources and transformations of a dataset or artifact.
concepts.label: Data lineage

concepts.definition: A mismatch between the data transformations or feature semantics used in training and serving.
concepts.label: Training-serving skew

concepts.definition: Identifying and managing repeated or near-duplicate examples.
concepts.label: Dataset deduplication

concepts.definition: Allocating learning effort to examples according to value, coverage, and acquisition cost.
concepts.label: Data selection

concepts.definition: Mapping text into vocabulary-dependent token identifiers, which sets sequence lengths and so influences context usage, embedding size, and processing cost.
concepts.label: Tokenization

concepts.definition: A difference between development and deployment data-generating distributions.
concepts.label: Distribution shift

concepts.definition: Models whose score is linear in their supplied features, with a possible output link function.
concepts.label: Linear models

concepts.definition: Collections of decision trees whose branch traversal and aggregation determine predictions.
concepts.label: Tree ensembles

concepts.definition: Models using similarity functions whose storage and evaluation costs depend on their representation.
concepts.label: Kernel methods

concepts.definition: Predictions or retrieval based on similarity to stored examples or vectors.
concepts.label: Nearest-neighbor models

concepts.definition: Parameterized compositions of differentiable operations used to learn representations and predictions.
concepts.label: Neural networks

concepts.definition: Structural assumptions that favor some learned functions over others.
concepts.label: Inductive bias

concepts.definition: Vector representations whose dimension and lookup or construction method affect storage and computation.
concepts.label: Embeddings

concepts.definition: Input-dependent aggregation of value vectors using query-key compatibility scores.
concepts.label: Attention

concepts.definition: Representations that make sequence position available to a model.
concepts.label: Position encoding

concepts.definition: A computable criterion optimized on training examples.
concepts.label: Training loss

concepts.definition: Computing derivatives by composing local derivative rules through an execution graph.
concepts.label: Automatic differentiation

concepts.definition: A rule that uses training information to update model parameters and optimizer state.
concepts.label: Optimization algorithm

concepts.definition: Constraints or training procedures used to control sensitivity and generalization behavior.
concepts.label: Regularization

concepts.definition: The number of examples contributing to an optimization update or microstep.
concepts.label: Training batch size

concepts.definition: The parameters, gradients, optimizer variables, and other state needed to continue training.
concepts.label: Training state

concepts.definition: Recreating forward intermediates during backward execution to reduce retained memory.
concepts.label: Activation recomputation

concepts.definition: Fitted relationships between resources, data, model size, and observed model performance.
concepts.label: Empirical scaling laws

concepts.definition: Choosing model or training settings through a sequence of evaluations.
concepts.label: Hyperparameter search

concepts.definition: Dividing a finite evaluation budget across configurations, repetitions, and fidelities.
concepts.label: Experiment-budget allocation

concepts.definition: Adapting representations or parameters learned from one setting to another.
concepts.label: Transfer learning

concepts.definition: Adapting a model by changing a limited parameter subset or added parameterization.
concepts.label: Parameter-efficient adaptation

concepts.definition: The mapping from tensor indices to storage locations, including strides and materialization.
concepts.label: Tensor layout

concepts.definition: A dense linear-algebra operation whose tiling, shape, and precision affect execution cost.
concepts.label: Matrix multiplication

concepts.definition: The representable values and arithmetic behavior of a numerical format.
concepts.label: Numerical precision

concepts.definition: Sensitivity of a computed result to finite-precision operations and intermediate representations.
concepts.label: Numerical stability

concepts.definition: Training with multiple numerical formats and explicit handling of their range and accumulation behavior.
concepts.label: Mixed-precision training

concepts.definition: Representing values using a reduced discrete set with a specified encoding and approximation rule.
concepts.label: Quantization

concepts.definition: A pattern of absent or zero values whose execution benefit depends on representation and support.
concepts.label: Sparsity

concepts.definition: Training a student model using signals from a teacher model or ensemble.
concepts.label: Knowledge distillation

concepts.definition: Transforming a model or execution graph into an executable representation.
concepts.label: Graph compilation

concepts.definition: Combining compatible operations to reduce intermediate materialization or dispatch.
concepts.label: Kernel fusion

concepts.definition: Host-side work required to launch or orchestrate device operations.
concepts.label: Host dispatch overhead

concepts.definition: Available storage for concurrently resident state and intermediates.
concepts.label: Memory capacity

concepts.definition: The sustainable rate at which bytes move across a specified memory interface.
concepts.label: Memory bandwidth

concepts.definition: The sustainable rate of a specified arithmetic workload on an execution resource.
concepts.label: Compute throughput

concepts.definition: Arithmetic work per byte transferred at a specified memory boundary.
concepts.label: Arithmetic intensity

concepts.definition: A performance bound combining a compute ceiling with an intensity-dependent bandwidth ceiling.
concepts.label: Roofline bound

concepts.definition: Reuse of data near its consumers across time or execution locations.
concepts.label: Data locality

concepts.definition: Partitioning computation so working data can be reused within a chosen storage level.
concepts.label: Tiling

concepts.definition: Measuring execution to attribute time, work, stalls, and resource use.
concepts.label: Profiling

concepts.definition: The fraction of a resource's defined service capacity that is occupied over a stated interval.
concepts.label: Resource utilization

concepts.definition: The portion of execution that a proposed parallel or accelerated transformation leaves unchanged.
concepts.label: Serial fraction

concepts.definition: Coordinated data exchange and reduction across a process group.
concepts.label: Collective communication

concepts.definition: Executing model replicas on different examples while coordinating learning state.
concepts.label: Data parallelism

concepts.definition: Partitioning a layer's tensors and operations across devices so each computes a slice, reducing per-device state while adding communication along the partitioned dimensions, usually within a fast scale-up domain.
concepts.label: Tensor parallelism

concepts.definition: Partitioning a computation into stages that process different microbatches concurrently.
concepts.label: Pipeline parallelism

concepts.definition: Partitioning parameters, gradients, or optimizer state across workers.
concepts.label: Training-state sharding

concepts.definition: Scheduling communication concurrently with independent computation.
concepts.label: Communication overlap

concepts.definition: The connectivity and capacity structure that constrains communication paths.
concepts.label: Network topology

concepts.definition: Workers or tasks whose delayed completion holds back coordinated work.
concepts.label: Stragglers

concepts.definition: A persisted state from which a specified computation can resume.
concepts.label: Recovery checkpoint

concepts.definition: A recoverable collection of distributed states with compatible dependencies.
concepts.label: Consistent checkpoint cut

concepts.definition: Agreement on an ordered state history under specified timing and failure assumptions.
concepts.label: Replicated-log consensus

concepts.definition: Rejecting effects from an actor whose epoch or authority is stale.
concepts.label: Fencing

concepts.definition: Coordinating model learning across separately controlled data holders.
concepts.label: Federated learning

concepts.definition: The frequency and distribution of requests reaching a service boundary.
concepts.label: Arrival rate

concepts.definition: The completion rate supported by a service under a stated workload and operating point.
concepts.label: Service capacity

concepts.definition: Time a request waits for a resource before receiving service.
concepts.label: Queueing delay

concepts.definition: A high quantile of a defined request-latency distribution.
concepts.label: Tail latency

concepts.definition: Executing requests together to share work or improve resource use.
concepts.label: Request batching

concepts.definition: Accepting, delaying, or rejecting work according to capacity, policy, and service constraints.
concepts.label: Admission control

concepts.definition: Changing provisioned service resources in response to measured or predicted demand.
concepts.label: Autoscaling

concepts.definition: Retained attention keys and values reused during autoregressive execution.
concepts.label: KV cache

concepts.definition: The prompt-processing and incremental token-generation phases of autoregressive inference.
concepts.label: Prefill and decode

concepts.definition: Managing attention state in blocks to reduce allocation waste and support sharing.
concepts.label: Paged KV allocation

concepts.definition: Reusing compatible computed state for an identical request prefix.
concepts.label: Prefix caching

concepts.definition: Using proposed tokens and a validating procedure to accelerate generation while preserving a specified output distribution.
concepts.label: Speculative decoding

concepts.definition: The rate of useful completed work that satisfies the specified quality and service criteria.
concepts.label: SLO goodput

concepts.definition: Performance on relevant examples or conditions beyond those used to fit the system.
concepts.label: Generalization

concepts.definition: A partitioning protocol that separates learning, selection, and final assessment.
concepts.label: Evaluation split

concepts.definition: Overstated performance caused by choosing a winner using noisy evaluation results.
concepts.label: Model-selection optimism

concepts.definition: Specified measurements of predictive or task behavior, with explicit populations and aggregation.
concepts.label: Evaluation metrics

concepts.definition: Agreement between predicted probabilities and observed event frequencies under an evaluation distribution.
concepts.label: Probability calibration

concepts.definition: Uncertainty in an estimated quantity due to finite and dependent observations.
concepts.label: Statistical uncertainty

concepts.definition: A reproducible workload, measurement boundary, and comparison procedure.
concepts.label: Benchmark protocol

concepts.definition: A controlled intervention used to estimate effects on deployed-system outcomes.
concepts.label: Online experimentation

concepts.definition: Measuring behavior separately on relevant populations, conditions, or workload groups.
concepts.label: Sliced evaluation

concepts.definition: Predicting on admitted cases and abstaining or deferring the rest.
concepts.label: Selective prediction

concepts.definition: Identifying the exact model, code, data, configuration, and dependencies in an execution or release.
concepts.label: Artifact versioning

concepts.definition: Collecting and interpreting signals about deployed system behavior and health.
concepts.label: Production monitoring

concepts.definition: Increasing exposure to a candidate system through bounded release stages.
concepts.label: Staged rollout

concepts.definition: Returning to a previously accepted deployment configuration with compatible state.
concepts.label: Rollback

concepts.definition: A deployed system's outputs changing the data or behavior encountered by future learning or evaluation.
concepts.label: Deployment feedback loop

concepts.definition: Training a replacement version of a deployed model on updated or revised data, with timing and data chosen to balance staleness against training and validation cost.
concepts.label: Retraining

concepts.definition: Detecting, containing, diagnosing, and recovering from unexpected system behavior.
concepts.label: Incident response

concepts.definition: Instrumentation that permits investigation of internal execution from recorded outputs, traces, and metrics.
concepts.label: System observability

concepts.definition: Specifying adversaries, assets, interfaces, capabilities, and failure consequences.
concepts.label: Threat modeling

concepts.definition: Adversarial manipulation of learning data or signals to alter learned behavior.
concepts.label: Data poisoning

concepts.definition: Adversarially chosen inference inputs intended to cause harmful model behavior.
concepts.label: Adversarial evasion

concepts.definition: Requirements governing the collection, use, retention, and disclosure of information about people or records.
concepts.label: Privacy requirements

concepts.definition: A parameterized bound on changes in output distributions under a specified neighboring-dataset relation.
concepts.label: Differential privacy

concepts.definition: Explicit requirements for how system outcomes or errors are distributed across affected groups.
concepts.label: Fairness criteria

concepts.definition: Determining whether an actor may perform a specified action on a resource.
concepts.label: Authorization

concepts.definition: Restricting which resources and effects a computation can access.
concepts.label: Execution isolation

concepts.definition: An arrangement in which people can understand, intervene in, and contest consequential system behavior.
concepts.label: Human oversight

concepts.definition: Energy consumed by a specified system boundary over a defined workload or interval.
concepts.label: Operating energy

concepts.definition: Emissions attributed to operation and embodied system resources under declared accounting boundaries.
concepts.label: Lifecycle carbon

concepts.definition: Total relevant expenditure divided by outcomes meeting a specified acceptance criterion.
concepts.label: Cost per useful outcome

concepts.definition: Provisioning resources for a workload distribution and service objectives.
concepts.label: Capacity planning

concepts.definition: A sequence of observations, model proposals, tool actions, and external outcomes for a task.
concepts.label: Agent trajectory

concepts.definition: Constructing and revising prospective actions in response to goals, dependencies, and observations.
concepts.label: Agent planning

concepts.definition: The maximum token span a model supports in a stated execution mode, bounding the history it can use and the longest sequences the system must process.
concepts.label: Context window

concepts.definition: Selecting relevant records from an external collection using an explicit query and ranking process.
concepts.label: Retrieval

concepts.definition: Trading exact neighbor recovery for reduced search cost using an index or approximation.
concepts.label: Approximate nearest-neighbor search

concepts.definition: Generated factual assertions or summaries not supported by the relevant source or evidence.
concepts.label: Hallucination

concepts.definition: A specification of tool inputs, outputs, authority, effects, and failure behavior.
concepts.label: Tool contract

concepts.definition: A specified operation's repeated execution having the same intended effect as one execution.
concepts.label: Idempotency

concepts.definition: An explicit action intended to remedy an earlier effect whose direct reversal is unavailable.
concepts.label: Compensating action

concepts.definition: Untrusted content attempting to redirect model-driven behavior across an instruction or authority boundary.
concepts.label: Prompt injection

concepts.definition: Assessing task outcomes, intermediate effects, and constraint compliance across a complete agent run.
concepts.label: Trajectory evaluation

concepts.definition: Improving a measured reward through behavior that fails the intended task objective.
concepts.label: Reward hacking

concepts.definition: The evolution of a physical system under inputs, disturbances, and constraints.
concepts.label: Physical dynamics

concepts.definition: Establishing how observations relate to physical quantities, coordinates, and time.
concepts.label: Sensor calibration

concepts.definition: Inferring latent physical state and uncertainty from observations and a model.
concepts.label: State estimation

concepts.definition: Whether distinct internal states can be distinguished through the available observations and model.
concepts.label: State observability

concepts.definition: Elapsed time between a physical observation and its use in a decision.
concepts.label: Observation age

concepts.definition: Delay around a sensing, computation, communication, and actuation loop.
concepts.label: Feedback delay

concepts.definition: A justified execution-time upper bound under specified hardware and execution assumptions.
concepts.label: Worst-case execution time

concepts.definition: Selecting inputs using measured or estimated deviation from desired behavior.
concepts.label: Feedback control

concepts.definition: Satisfaction of motion, state, input, and dynamic constraints along a proposed trajectory.
concepts.label: Trajectory feasibility

concepts.definition: Mechanical interaction whose forces depend on geometry, motion, stiffness, and damping.
concepts.label: Contact and compliance

concepts.definition: Deployment of a learned policy under differences between simulated and physical conditions.
concepts.label: Simulation-to-real transfer

concepts.definition: Monitoring and constraining execution using explicitly stated safety premises and fallback mechanisms.
concepts.label: Runtime assurance

concepts.definition: The state and clearance conditions within which a specified stopping response remains feasible.
concepts.label: Stopping envelope

concepts.definition: The conditions under which a physical system's behavior and evidence are intended to apply.
concepts.label: Operational design domain

concepts.definition: A structured argument connecting claims, evidence, assumptions, and defeaters for a defined system.
concepts.label: Safety case

concepts.definition: Restricting the syntax or schema of model outputs without establishing factual correctness or authority.
concepts.label: Structured output constraint

concepts.definition: The observation and selection process that determines which examples and populations enter a dataset.
concepts.label: Data acquisition and sampling

concepts.definition: A specification of schema, semantics, validity rules, and availability for data exchanged between components.
concepts.label: Data contract

concepts.definition: Target outcomes that become observable only after a delay or for a selected subset of cases.
concepts.label: Delayed outcomes

concepts.definition: The rule that converts model outputs and system state into actions, thresholds, abstentions, or escalation.
concepts.label: Decision policy

concepts.definition: Testing behavior under explicitly chosen shifts, perturbations, faults, or operating stresses.
concepts.label: Robustness evaluation

concepts.definition: Learning a prediction rule from examples with target outputs.
concepts.label: Supervised learning

concepts.definition: Learning from targets constructed from the observed data itself.
concepts.label: Self-supervised learning

concepts.definition: Learning structure in data without externally supplied example-level targets.
concepts.label: Unsupervised learning

concepts.definition: Learning a policy from action-dependent observations and reward signals.
concepts.label: Reinforcement learning

concepts.definition: Learning a policy from demonstrated behavior and possibly corrective interaction.
concepts.label: Imitation learning

concepts.definition: The learned parameters, structures, example stores, and metadata required to execute a model.
concepts.label: Model artifact

concepts.definition: The declared classes of faults and timing assumptions under which a mechanism is analyzed.
concepts.label: Failure model

concepts.definition: A mechanism that signals downstream saturation to limit or slow upstream production.
concepts.label: Backpressure

concepts.definition: Information about people or records revealed through data, artifacts, or model interaction.
concepts.label: Privacy leakage

concepts.definition: Elapsed time for a specified execution boundary, workload, and operating condition.
concepts.label: Execution time

concepts.definition: External consequences that cannot be fully undone by restoring software state, retrying, or performing a compensating action.
concepts.label: Irreversible effects

concepts.definition: Organization of stored dataset records, columns, partitions, and metadata that determines which data an access reads or decodes.
concepts.label: Dataset storage layout

concepts.definition: Reading externally produced records into a processing or learning system under declared delivery, ordering, and timing assumptions.
concepts.label: Data ingestion

concepts.definition: Changing a data schema while explicitly managing how existing data and producers or consumers remain interpretable and compatible.
concepts.label: Schema evolution

concepts.definition: A specification, procedure, reference, or informed judgment used to assess whether observed behavior satisfies stated expectations for a test.
concepts.label: Test oracle

concepts.definition: Testing interactions among assembled components against stated interface and behavior expectations.
concepts.label: Integration testing

concepts.definition: Deliberately introducing selected faults or disruptive conditions to observe system response under controlled experimental boundaries.
concepts.label: Failure injection

concepts.definition: The software packages, versions, native libraries, and runtime configuration on which an execution depends.
concepts.label: Dependency environment

concepts.definition: Coordinating dependent computation steps, their data or control flow, execution conditions, and failure handling.
concepts.label: Workflow orchestration

concepts.definition: The ability to repeat an experimental procedure and obtain results consistent with declared criteria when its inputs, environment, randomness, and execution conditions are specified.
concepts.label: Experiment reproducibility

concepts.definition: Organization of arithmetic units, execution lanes or threads, scheduling resources, and local storage that determines how supported operations run. SIMD/SIMT, matrix units, and systolic arrays are distinct examples.
concepts.label: Accelerator execution architecture

concepts.definition: Arrangement of storage levels and transfer paths with differing capacity, latency, bandwidth, access control, and management mechanisms. The available levels depend on the platform.
concepts.label: Memory hierarchy

concepts.definition: Communication path through which a host and accelerator exchange data and control, with transport, topology, and memory-access semantics that affect transfers.
concepts.label: Host-device interconnect

concepts.definition: Supply paths, conversion stages, limits, and transient behavior that must maintain required voltages while workloads and actuators draw or return power.
concepts.label: Power delivery and integrity

concepts.definition: Evolution of temperature under heat generation and removal, and the performance controls or operating restrictions that follow under a platform thermal policy.
concepts.label: Thermal behavior and throttling

concepts.definition: A quantitative measure of one aspect of delivered service, such as latency, availability, or accepted-output rate, computed over a stated population and window.
concepts.label: Service-level indicator

concepts.definition: The amount of service-level-objective violation permitted over a window, used to pace changes and risk against a reliability target.
concepts.label: Error budget

concepts.definition: An allocation of an end-to-end latency target across the stages of a request path, such as network, preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing.
concepts.label: Latency budget

concepts.definition: Estimating a workload's arithmetic operations and bytes moved per example, token, or step from model shapes, to predict cost before measurement.
concepts.label: Operation and byte accounting

concepts.definition: The peak memory a workload occupies, summed over parameters, activations, optimizer or cache state, and runtime buffers.
concepts.label: Memory footprint

concepts.definition: A recorded sequence of requests or jobs with arrival times, sizes, and durations, replayed to evaluate capacity, scheduling, or serving policies.
concepts.label: Workload trace

concepts.definition: Choosing actions or thresholds to minimize expected cost when different error types carry unequal consequences.
concepts.label: Cost-sensitive decision

concepts.definition: The set of configurations for which no objective, such as accuracy, latency, or cost, can improve without worsening another.
concepts.label: Pareto frontier

concepts.definition: A neural architecture of stacked attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections and normalization, processing all sequence positions in parallel during training.
concepts.label: Transformer

concepts.definition: Models combining large sparse embedding tables for categorical features with dense layers, whose cost is often dominated by embedding lookups and memory capacity.
concepts.label: Deep recommendation model

concepts.definition: A generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process, producing samples through many iterative denoising network evaluations.
concepts.label: Diffusion model

concepts.definition: A locally connected operation applying shared filters across spatial or temporal positions, giving high weight reuse and arithmetic intensity.
concepts.label: Convolution

concepts.definition: Computation that updates a hidden state step by step over a sequence, creating sequential dependencies that limit parallelism across time.
concepts.label: Recurrent computation

concepts.definition: Layers that rescale activations using batch, layer, or root-mean-square statistics to stabilize and speed training of deep networks.
concepts.label: Normalization layers

concepts.definition: An architecture in which a learned router activates a small subset of expert subnetworks per token, decoupling total parameter count from per-token compute.
concepts.label: Mixture of experts

concepts.definition: The gating function that assigns each token to one or more experts, such as top-k softmax gating or expert-choice routing.
concepts.label: Expert routing

concepts.definition: The maximum number of tokens an expert processes per batch, set by a capacity factor; tokens beyond it are dropped or rerouted.
concepts.label: Expert capacity

concepts.definition: An auxiliary training objective that penalizes uneven token assignment across experts so routing stays balanced.
concepts.label: Load-balancing loss

concepts.definition: The parameters actually used to process one token or example, as distinct from total stored parameters in conditionally computed models.
concepts.label: Active parameters

concepts.definition: Terminating inference at an intermediate layer once a confidence criterion is met, so per-input compute varies with input difficulty.
concepts.label: Early exit

concepts.definition: Attention restricted to local windows or fixed sparse patterns so cost grows linearly rather than quadratically with sequence length.
concepts.label: Sparse and sliding-window attention

concepts.definition: Attention reformulated with kernel feature maps so it is computed in linear time with a fixed-size recurrent state.
concepts.label: Linear attention

concepts.definition: Sequence models built on discretized linear state-space recurrences, trainable in parallel and run with constant-size state per step at inference.
concepts.label: State-space sequence model

concepts.definition: Attention in which groups of query heads share key and value heads, shrinking the key-value cache and decode memory traffic.
concepts.label: Grouped-query attention

concepts.definition: Techniques that extend a trained model's usable sequence length, such as position-encoding interpolation followed by long-sequence fine-tuning.
concepts.label: Context-length extension

concepts.definition: The on-disk encoding of a model's parameter tensors and metadata, governing load time, memory mapping, and safety of deserialization.
concepts.label: Weight serialization format

concepts.definition: A framework-neutral representation of a model's operator graph and weights used to move models between training frameworks and inference runtimes.
concepts.label: Model exchange format

concepts.definition: Converting a framework program into a self-contained deployable artifact by tracing or capturing its graph and fixing operators, shapes, and weights.
concepts.label: Model export

concepts.definition: The declared names, types, and shapes of a model artifact's inputs and outputs, forming its interface contract with callers.
concepts.label: Model signature

concepts.definition: The arithmetic intensity at which a roofline's bandwidth and compute ceilings meet, equal to peak compute throughput divided by peak memory bandwidth.
concepts.label: Ridge point

concepts.definition: Classifying a kernel or phase by which roofline ceiling limits it, indicating whether more arithmetic throughput or more bandwidth would help.
concepts.label: Compute-bound vs. memory-bound

concepts.definition: The energy cost of moving operands between storage levels, which grows with distance and typically exceeds the energy of the arithmetic performed on them.
concepts.label: Data-movement energy

concepts.definition: The bound that overall speedup from accelerating part of an execution is limited by the fraction left unaccelerated.
concepts.label: Amdahl's law

concepts.definition: How time to solution changes as resources increase for a fixed total problem size.
concepts.label: Strong scaling

concepts.definition: How time to solution changes as resources and problem size grow proportionally, keeping work per resource fixed.
concepts.label: Weak scaling

concepts.definition: Achieved speedup divided by the factor of added resources, measuring how much additional hardware turns into useful progress.
concepts.label: Parallel scaling efficiency

concepts.definition: The relation that the mean number of items in a stable system equals mean arrival rate times mean time in the system.
concepts.label: Little's law

concepts.definition: The relationship between offered load and latency, in which queueing delay grows sharply as utilization approaches capacity.
concepts.label: Latency-throughput curve

concepts.definition: Variability of request inter-arrival times or sizes beyond a Poisson baseline, which raises queueing delay at a given mean utilization.
concepts.label: Arrival burstiness

concepts.definition: Choosing model size and training data quantity to minimize loss under a fixed training compute budget, using fitted scaling laws.
concepts.label: Compute-optimal allocation

concepts.definition: Approximating dense transformer training compute as roughly six floating-point operations per parameter per training token.
concepts.label: Training compute estimate

concepts.definition: A grid of processing elements that pass operands rhythmically to neighbors, performing matrix multiplication with high operand reuse and little register-file traffic.
concepts.label: Systolic array

concepts.definition: A functional unit that executes small dense matrix multiply-accumulate tiles per instruction, supplying most of an accelerator's peak low-precision throughput.
concepts.label: Matrix engine

concepts.definition: An execution model in which groups of threads issue common instructions to active lanes, with divergent paths executed under lane masks and architecture-specific reconvergence.
concepts.label: SIMT execution

concepts.definition: The mapping that decides which operands stay resident in local storage while others stream, such as weight-, output-, or row-stationary schedules.
concepts.label: Accelerator dataflow

concepts.definition: Hardware specialized to a class of workloads, trading programmability for higher performance per watt on its target operations.
concepts.label: Domain-specific architecture

concepts.definition: Stacked DRAM placed beside the processor on an interposer, providing very high bandwidth with limited capacity per stack.
concepts.label: High-bandwidth memory

concepts.definition: Small, fast on-die storage, such as caches, shared memory, and register files, used to stage reused operands near compute units.
concepts.label: On-chip SRAM and scratchpads

concepts.definition: The widening gap between processor arithmetic throughput and memory bandwidth or latency, which makes data movement the limiting factor.
concepts.label: Memory wall

concepts.definition: High-bandwidth links and switches, such as NVLink-class fabrics, joining accelerators within a node or rack into one tightly coupled domain.
concepts.label: Scale-up interconnect

concepts.definition: A link protocol that lets hosts and devices share or pool memory with hardware coherence, such as CXL over a PCIe physical layer.
concepts.label: Cache-coherent interconnect

concepts.definition: Direct memory access between accelerators, or between accelerators and NICs or storage, without staging data through host memory.
concepts.label: Peer-to-peer device transfer

concepts.definition: The sustained heat dissipation a cooling solution is designed to remove, used as a chip's nominal power envelope.
concepts.label: Thermal design power

concepts.definition: Adjusting supply voltage and clock frequency at runtime to trade performance for power, since dynamic power grows superlinearly with voltage.
concepts.label: Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling

concepts.definition: The fraction of a chip that cannot be powered at full frequency simultaneously within its power and thermal budget.
concepts.label: Dark silicon

concepts.definition: Enforcing a maximum power draw on a device or group by limiting clocks or activity, trading peak throughput for bounded power.
concepts.label: Power capping

concepts.definition: A low-power processor with on-chip flash and kilobytes to a few megabytes of SRAM, typically without an operating system or virtual memory.
concepts.label: Microcontroller-class device

concepts.definition: A system-on-chip combining CPU, GPU, DSP, and NPU blocks under shared memory and power limits, across which model operators are partitioned.
concepts.label: Heterogeneous mobile SoC

concepts.definition: An accelerator integrated in mobile or embedded silicon for low-precision neural inference, usually supporting a restricted set of operators.
concepts.label: On-device neural accelerator

concepts.definition: Energy consumed to process one input end to end on a device, the binding metric for battery-powered and energy-harvesting deployments.
concepts.label: Energy per inference

concepts.definition: The flash and SRAM limits that bound a deployed model's stored weights and peak activation memory on embedded hardware.
concepts.label: On-device memory budget

concepts.definition: A multidimensional array carrying shape, element type, device, and layout metadata, the core data abstraction of ML frameworks.
concepts.label: Tensor

concepts.definition: A directed graph of tensor operations and their data dependencies representing a model program, used for differentiation, optimization, and scheduling.
concepts.label: Computation graph

concepts.definition: The choice between running each operation as the host program issues it and building a whole graph first for later optimization and execution.
concepts.label: Eager vs. graph execution

concepts.definition: Recording operations executed on example inputs to build a graph compiled just in time, with guards or retracing when shapes or control flow change.
concepts.label: Tracing and JIT capture

concepts.definition: An exact attention implementation that tiles queries, keys, and values through on-chip memory to avoid materializing the full score matrix in off-chip memory.
concepts.label: IO-aware attention kernel

concepts.definition: Implementing convolution by rearranging input patches into matrices for GEMM, or by direct, FFT, or Winograd algorithms with different memory costs.
concepts.label: Convolution lowering

concepts.definition: Tuned implementations of common operators supplied for a hardware platform, which frameworks call rather than generating their own kernels.
concepts.label: Vendor kernel library

concepts.definition: Program representations at graph, tensor, and loop levels on which compilers apply lowering and optimization passes.
concepts.label: ML compiler IR

concepts.definition: Searching kernel schedule parameters, such as tile sizes and loop orders, by measurement or learned cost models to find fast implementations for a target.
concepts.label: Kernel autotuning

concepts.definition: A domain-specific language for writing tiled tensor kernels above the level of vendor assembly, with the compiler handling memory and thread mapping.
concepts.label: Kernel DSL

concepts.definition: Compile-time assignment of tensor buffers to memory with lifetime-based reuse, reducing peak memory and runtime allocation.
concepts.label: Static memory planning

concepts.definition: Ordered queues of device work that the host enqueues asynchronously, with events expressing dependencies and allowing overlap across queues.
concepts.label: Device streams

concepts.definition: A runtime allocator that retains and reuses freed device memory blocks to avoid costly allocation calls, at the risk of fragmentation.
concepts.label: Caching memory allocator

concepts.definition: Recording a fixed sequence of kernel launches once and replaying it as a unit to remove per-launch host overhead.
concepts.label: Captured graph replay

concepts.definition: Multiplying the loss before backpropagation so small gradients remain representable in reduced-precision formats, then unscaling before the optimizer step.
concepts.label: Loss scaling

concepts.definition: Low-precision formats in which small blocks of values share a scale factor, extending dynamic range for FP8, FP6, FP4, or INT8 elements.
concepts.label: Block-scaled number formats

concepts.definition: The numerical format used to sum products in dot products and reductions, which may differ from input precision and governs rounding-error growth.
concepts.label: Accumulation precision

concepts.definition: Placing different experts of a mixture-of-experts layer on different devices and exchanging routed tokens among them.
concepts.label: Expert parallelism

concepts.definition: Partitioning activations along the sequence dimension across devices, exchanging keys, values, or partial results so long sequences fit.
concepts.label: Sequence and context parallelism

concepts.definition: Combining data, tensor, pipeline, and other parallelism dimensions, mapped onto the hardware hierarchy so the most communication-intensive dimension uses the fastest links.
concepts.label: Hybrid parallelism

concepts.definition: Idle device time during pipeline fill and drain, whose fraction shrinks as the number of microbatches grows relative to pipeline stages.
concepts.label: Pipeline bubble

concepts.definition: An all-reduce performed as reduce-scatter then all-gather around a ring, bandwidth-optimal for large messages but with latency linear in participants.
concepts.label: Ring all-reduce

concepts.definition: All-reduce schedules over trees or hierarchical groups, with latency logarithmic in participants, suited to small messages and multi-level networks.
concepts.label: Tree and hierarchical all-reduce

concepts.definition: A collective in which every participant sends distinct data to every other, as in expert routing; its throughput is sensitive to bisection bandwidth.
concepts.label: All-to-all exchange

concepts.definition: A cost model estimating message time as a fixed latency term plus message size times a per-byte cost, used to compare collective algorithms.
concepts.label: Alpha-beta communication model

concepts.definition: Reducing gradient communication through quantization, sparsification, or low-rank approximation, often with error feedback to preserve convergence.
concepts.label: Gradient compression

concepts.definition: A time-bounded grant of authority or cached state that expires unless renewed, letting a system recover from failed holders without explicit release.
concepts.label: Lease

concepts.definition: Selecting a single coordinator among replicas, typically through consensus and leases, so control decisions have one authoritative source.
concepts.label: Leader election

concepts.definition: A consistency model in which workers may compute on parameters up to a fixed number of updates old, trading freshness for less waiting.
concepts.label: Bounded staleness

concepts.definition: A federated algorithm in which sampled clients run several local optimization steps and a server averages their model updates, weighted by data size.
concepts.label: Federated averaging

concepts.definition: Differences in data distribution and quantity across federated clients, which slow convergence and can bias a shared model.
concepts.label: Statistical heterogeneity

concepts.definition: Choosing which available devices participate in each federated round, subject to availability, connectivity, and power constraints.
concepts.label: Client selection

concepts.definition: The distinction between federations of many intermittently available devices and federations of a few reliable organizational data holders.
concepts.label: Cross-device vs. cross-silo federation

concepts.definition: Total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy, measuring overhead from cooling, power conversion, and other non-compute loads.
concepts.label: Power usage effectiveness

concepts.definition: Removing heat with liquid through cold plates or immersion, enabling rack power densities beyond the practical limits of air cooling.
concepts.label: Liquid cooling

concepts.definition: Electrical power drawn per rack, which determines cooling technology, floor layout, and how many accelerators fit within a facility's power envelope.
concepts.label: Rack power density

concepts.definition: Deploying more equipment than the sum of nameplate power a feed supports, relying on non-coincident peaks and power capping to stay within limits.
concepts.label: Power oversubscription

concepts.definition: A datacenter treated as a single computer whose power, cooling, network, and software are co-designed for a common workload.
concepts.label: Warehouse-scale computer

concepts.definition: Network transfers that read or write remote memory directly through the network interface without remote CPU involvement, giving low latency and high throughput.
concepts.label: Remote direct memory access

concepts.definition: A network that avoids packet drops through credit-based or priority flow control, as RDMA transports expect, at the risk of head-of-line blocking.
concepts.label: Lossless network fabric

concepts.definition: End-host and switch mechanisms, such as ECN-driven rate control, that limit queue buildup from incast and synchronized collective traffic.
concepts.label: Datacenter congestion control

concepts.definition: A multistage switch topology providing many equal-cost paths and, without oversubscription, full bisection bandwidth between endpoints.
concepts.label: Fat-tree (Clos) topology

concepts.definition: A fabric design connecting the same-index accelerator of every node to a common leaf switch, keeping most collective traffic within one switch hop.
concepts.label: Rail-optimized topology

concepts.definition: The minimum total bandwidth across any cut dividing a network into two equal halves, bounding throughput of all-to-all and global exchanges.
concepts.label: Bisection bandwidth

concepts.definition: Performing collective reductions inside network switches so data crosses each link fewer times, lowering all-reduce traffic and latency.
concepts.label: In-network reduction

concepts.definition: A distributed file system that stripes data across many storage servers to deliver aggregate bandwidth to many concurrent clients.
concepts.label: Parallel file system

concepts.definition: Storage of immutable named objects behind an HTTP-style interface, offering scalable capacity and throughput with higher per-request latency than file systems.
concepts.label: Object storage

concepts.definition: The read, decode, transform, shuffle, and prefetch stages that deliver batches to accelerators; when slower than compute, they cause data stalls.
concepts.label: Training input pipeline

concepts.definition: Writing and reading large training-state snapshots, where storage bandwidth, asynchronous persistence, and sharded layout determine checkpoint cost.
concepts.label: Checkpoint I/O

concepts.definition: Placing data across tiers, from memory and local NVMe caches to shared and archival storage, according to access frequency and cost.
concepts.label: Storage tiering and caching

concepts.definition: Allocating all resources a parallel job needs at once, or none, so tightly coupled workers start together and partial allocations cannot deadlock.
concepts.label: Gang scheduling

concepts.definition: Suspending or evicting a running job to reclaim its resources for higher-priority work, at a cost set by checkpointing and lost progress.
concepts.label: Job preemption

concepts.definition: A multi-resource fair-sharing policy that equalizes each user's largest share across resource types such as accelerators, CPUs, and memory.
concepts.label: Dominant resource fairness

concepts.definition: Training that continues while the number of workers changes, resharding state and adjusting batch size or learning rate as resources join or leave.
concepts.label: Elastic training

concepts.definition: Assigning a job's workers to devices and nodes so that heavily communicating groups share fast links or switches.
concepts.label: Topology-aware placement

concepts.definition: Placing jobs onto nodes to minimize fragmentation of resources such as accelerators, trading packing density against interference and locality.
concepts.label: Bin packing

concepts.definition: Sharing infrastructure among teams, jobs, or customers under policies for allocation, isolation, priority, and accounting.
concepts.label: Multi-tenancy

concepts.definition: A limit on the resources a tenant may hold or request, sometimes with guaranteed minimums and borrowing of idle capacity.
concepts.label: Resource quota

concepts.definition: Running several workloads on one accelerator by time-slicing, concurrent contexts, or hardware partitions with dedicated memory and compute slices.
concepts.label: Accelerator sharing and partitioning

concepts.definition: Discounted compute that the provider may reclaim at short notice, usable by workloads that tolerate interruption.
concepts.label: Spot and preemptible capacity

concepts.definition: Slowdown of one workload caused by co-located workloads contending for shared caches, memory bandwidth, network, or power.
concepts.label: Performance interference

concepts.definition: Producing training labels from noisy programmatic sources such as heuristics, rules, or distant supervision, then modeling and combining their errors.
concepts.label: Weak supervision

concepts.definition: Selecting which unlabeled examples to annotate next according to their expected value to the model.
concepts.label: Active learning

concepts.definition: The degree to which independent annotators assign the same label to the same item, used to measure label reliability and task ambiguity.
concepts.label: Inter-annotator agreement

concepts.definition: Removing or down-weighting training examples judged low quality by heuristics, classifiers, or model scores.
concepts.label: Quality filtering

concepts.definition: The proportions in which source domains or datasets are sampled during training.
concepts.label: Data mixture

concepts.definition: Training or evaluation examples generated by simulators, programs, or models rather than collected from the target environment.
concepts.label: Synthetic data

concepts.definition: Creating additional training examples by applying label-preserving transformations to existing ones.
concepts.label: Data augmentation

concepts.definition: Automated checks of incoming data against expected schema, value ranges, and distributions before it is used for training or serving.
concepts.label: Data validation

concepts.definition: A system that defines, computes, stores, and serves features consistently for offline training and online inference.
concepts.label: Feature store

concepts.definition: Continuously transforming unbounded event streams with low latency and incrementally maintained state.
concepts.label: Stream processing

concepts.definition: Recomputing a feature's historical values under a new or corrected definition so training data matches what serving will produce.
concepts.label: Feature backfill

concepts.definition: Recording immutable, addressable versions of datasets so that a training run or evaluation can identify exactly which data it used.
concepts.label: Dataset versioning

concepts.definition: Undeclared, unstable, or underused input signals on which a model depends, which can change or break its behavior silently.
concepts.label: Data dependency debt

concepts.definition: The age of a feature value at the time it is used for a prediction, relative to the freshness assumed during training.
concepts.label: Feature freshness

concepts.definition: The planned variation of the optimizer step size over training, such as warmup followed by decay.
concepts.label: Learning-rate schedule

concepts.definition: The batch size beyond which increasing it further yields diminishing reductions in optimization steps to reach a target loss.
concepts.label: Critical batch size

concepts.definition: Loss spikes, divergence, or collapse during training, often mitigated by gradient clipping, schedule changes, normalization, or restarting from a checkpoint.
concepts.label: Training instability

concepts.definition: Summing gradients over several micro-batches before one optimizer update to emulate a larger batch within limited memory.
concepts.label: Gradient accumulation

concepts.definition: Moving optimizer state, parameters, or activations from accelerator memory to host memory or storage between uses.
concepts.label: Training-state offloading

concepts.definition: Recording each run's code, data, configuration, metrics, and artifacts in a queryable store for comparison and reproduction.
concepts.label: Experiment tracking

concepts.definition: Tuning hyperparameters on smaller proxy models and reusing them at larger scale under a parameterization designed to keep them stable.
concepts.label: Hyperparameter transfer

concepts.definition: Continued training of a pretrained model on input-output demonstrations, such as instruction-response pairs, to shape task behavior.
concepts.label: Supervised fine-tuning

concepts.definition: Fine-tuning by learning low-rank update matrices added to frozen pretrained weights.
concepts.label: Low-rank adaptation

concepts.definition: Optimizing a model's policy against a reward model trained on human preference comparisons, usually with a penalty for drifting from a reference model.
concepts.label: RL from human feedback

concepts.definition: A learned model that scores outputs or trajectories to supply the training signal for policy optimization.
concepts.label: Reward model

concepts.definition: Training a policy directly on preferred-versus-rejected output pairs with a classification-style loss, without a separate reward model or RL loop.
concepts.label: Direct preference optimization

concepts.definition: Reinforcement learning whose rewards come from programmatic outcome checks, making verifier correctness and reward computation part of the training system.
concepts.label: RL with verifiable rewards

concepts.definition: Sampling responses or trajectories from the current policy, often with an inference engine, to produce experience for policy updates.
concepts.label: RL rollout generation

concepts.definition: Transferring updated policy weights from training workers to rollout workers, whose cost and frequency shape RL post-training throughput.
concepts.label: Policy weight synchronization

concepts.definition: The lag between the policy version that generated rollouts and the version being updated, introduced by asynchronous rollout and training.
concepts.label: Policy staleness

concepts.definition: Updating a model incrementally as each example or small batch arrives, rather than retraining on a fixed dataset.
concepts.label: Online learning

concepts.definition: Continuing training of an existing model from its current weights on new data instead of training from scratch.
concepts.label: Incremental training

concepts.definition: Loss of previously learned capability when a model is trained on new data or tasks.
concepts.label: Catastrophic forgetting

concepts.definition: Mixing stored past examples into updates on new data to reduce forgetting or reuse experience.
concepts.label: Experience replay

concepts.definition: Updating model parameters on the deployment device using local data under its memory, energy, and compute limits.
concepts.label: On-device training

concepts.definition: Estimating performance by repeatedly training on some data partitions and evaluating on the held-out remainder.
concepts.label: Cross-validation

concepts.definition: Experimental analysis that permits repeated looks at accumulating data while controlling error rates, unlike fixed-horizon tests.
concepts.label: Sequential testing

concepts.definition: Treatment of one experimental unit affecting outcomes of another, violating the no-interference assumption (SUTVA) of standard A/B analysis.
concepts.label: Experiment interference

concepts.definition: Constructing prediction sets with finite-sample coverage guarantees under exchangeability, using held-out calibration scores.
concepts.label: Conformal prediction

concepts.definition: Automatically finding coherent data subsets on which a model underperforms, without predefined slice labels.
concepts.label: Slice discovery

concepts.definition: Using a language model to score or compare generated outputs against a rubric, with its own biases and error rates to be measured.
concepts.label: Model-based grading

concepts.definition: The probability that at least one of k sampled outputs satisfies a correctness check.
concepts.label: pass@k

concepts.definition: Ranking models from judgments of which of two outputs is better, typically aggregated with a Bradley-Terry or Elo-style model.
concepts.label: Pairwise preference evaluation

concepts.definition: Assessment of system outputs by people following a protocol, used where automatic metrics or model graders are not trusted.
concepts.label: Human evaluation

concepts.definition: Presence of evaluation items, or close variants, in a model's training data, inflating measured performance.
concepts.label: Benchmark contamination

concepts.definition: Wall-clock time for a system to train a specified model to a specified quality target under fixed run rules.
concepts.label: Time to train

concepts.definition: A specified query-arrival pattern and latency constraint, such as single-stream, server, or offline, under which inference performance is measured.
concepts.label: Inference load scenario

concepts.definition: Testing by checking that known relations hold between outputs for related inputs, when correct outputs for single inputs are unknown.
concepts.label: Metamorphic testing

concepts.definition: Testing model capabilities with targeted input suites for invariance, directional change, and minimum functionality, independent of aggregate accuracy.
concepts.label: Behavioral testing

concepts.definition: A structured rubric of data, model, infrastructure, and monitoring tests used to judge whether an ML system is ready to operate.
concepts.label: Production-readiness assessment

concepts.definition: Producing predictions on demand for individual requests within a latency target.
concepts.label: Online inference

concepts.definition: Computing predictions for many inputs in scheduled jobs and storing them for later lookup.
concepts.label: Batch inference

concepts.definition: A service that loads model artifacts and executes inference requests behind a network interface, managing versions, batching, and resources.
concepts.label: Model server

concepts.definition: Hosting many models or adapters on shared serving resources, trading isolation and load time against utilization.
concepts.label: Multi-model serving

concepts.definition: Sending a request to cheaper models first and escalating to more capable models only when a confidence or quality criterion is not met.
concepts.label: Model cascade

concepts.definition: Choosing which model serves each request from request features, predicted quality, and cost.
concepts.label: Model routing

concepts.definition: Latency from request arrival until the first generated token is returned, dominated by queueing and prefill.
concepts.label: Time to first token

concepts.definition: For a request producing multiple tokens, its elapsed decoding time after the first output divided by its remaining generated-token count, summarizing average decoding speed at a declared measurement boundary.
concepts.label: Time per output token

concepts.definition: Issuing a duplicate request to another replica when the first has not responded within a delay, and using whichever returns first.
concepts.label: Hedged requests

concepts.definition: Scheduling at each generation iteration so finished sequences leave and new requests join a running batch.
concepts.label: Continuous batching

concepts.definition: Distributing requests across replicas according to load, locality, or cached state.
concepts.label: Request load balancing

concepts.definition: Delay before a newly started replica can serve, from provisioning, loading weights, and warming runtime state.
concepts.label: Model cold start

concepts.definition: Splitting a long prompt's prefill into chunks interleaved with decode steps to bound per-iteration latency.
concepts.label: Chunked prefill

concepts.definition: Running prefill and decode on separate resource pools, transferring KV state between them, so each phase is provisioned and batched independently.
concepts.label: Prefill-decode disaggregation

concepts.definition: Parameters and rules, such as greedy, temperature, top-k, and nucleus sampling, that determine how tokens are chosen from a model's distribution.
concepts.label: Decoding and sampling controls

concepts.definition: Masking disallowed tokens at each step, typically from a grammar or schema automaton, so output satisfies a structural constraint.
concepts.label: Constrained decoding

concepts.definition: Checking generated output against a schema or rules after generation and repairing, retrying, or rejecting it on failure.
concepts.label: Output validation

concepts.definition: A limit on the intermediate tokens or steps a model may spend before answering, set to trade quality against latency and cost.
concepts.label: Reasoning budget

concepts.definition: Generating n candidate outputs and returning the one ranked highest by a scorer or verifier.
concepts.label: Best-of-n sampling

concepts.definition: Sampling multiple reasoning paths and returning the most frequent final answer.
concepts.label: Self-consistency voting

concepts.definition: A model or program that judges whether a candidate output or reasoning step is correct, used for selection, search, or reward.
concepts.label: Verifier

concepts.definition: A verifier that scores intermediate reasoning steps rather than only final answers.
concepts.label: Process reward model

concepts.definition: Exploring a tree of partial solutions, as in beam or tree search, guided by a scorer, to find a higher-quality output.
concepts.label: Inference-time search

concepts.definition: The empirical relation between inference compute spent per query and output quality, used to allocate compute between model size and inference.
concepts.label: Test-time scaling

concepts.definition: Conditioning generation on documents retrieved for the request so outputs can draw on information outside the model's parameters.
concepts.label: Retrieval-augmented generation

concepts.definition: Retrieving records by similarity between learned embeddings of query and records.
concepts.label: Dense retrieval

concepts.definition: Retrieving records by weighted term overlap with the query using an inverted index, as in BM25.
concepts.label: Lexical retrieval

concepts.definition: Reordering a retrieved candidate set with a more expensive relevance model before use.
concepts.label: Reranking

concepts.definition: Translating a trained model into the format and operator set of a target runtime, possibly changing numerics and supported operations.
concepts.label: Model conversion

concepts.definition: An interpreter or compiled engine that executes models locally on personal or embedded devices, including inside browsers, under the target environment's memory, operator, and execution limits.
concepts.label: On-device inference runtime

concepts.definition: Delivering new model versions to deployed devices remotely, with staging, verification, and rollback across the device fleet.
concepts.label: Over-the-air model update

concepts.definition: Splitting inference between device and server, by layer or by model, to balance latency, energy, bandwidth, and privacy.
concepts.label: Device-cloud partitioning

concepts.definition: Variation in hardware, operating system, and runtime capability across a deployed device fleet that a single model release must accommodate.
concepts.label: Device heterogeneity

concepts.definition: A versioned store of model artifacts with metadata, lineage, and lifecycle stage used to govern promotion and deployment.
concepts.label: Model registry

concepts.definition: Running a candidate model on live traffic without serving its outputs, to compare it against the production model.
concepts.label: Shadow deployment

concepts.definition: Automated building, testing, and deployment of ML code, data checks, and model artifacts on each change.
concepts.label: CI/CD for ML

concepts.definition: A predeclared set of checks a candidate model must pass before it advances to a wider deployment stage.
concepts.label: Release gate

concepts.definition: Statistical tests or distances comparing production and reference distributions of inputs, predictions, or outcomes to flag change.
concepts.label: Drift detection

concepts.definition: Recording requests, model versions, outputs, and later outcomes so production behavior can be analyzed, debugged, and reused as data.
concepts.label: Prediction logging

concepts.definition: Rules that turn monitored signals into notifications for responders, tuned to balance missed incidents against alert fatigue.
concepts.label: Alerting

concepts.definition: Change over time in the relationship between inputs and targets, so the same input warrants a different prediction.
concepts.label: Concept drift

concepts.definition: An automated pipeline that retrains, validates, and proposes models on a schedule or when triggered by data or performance signals.
concepts.label: Continuous training

concepts.definition: A written analysis after an incident of its timeline, causes, and corrective actions, focused on system fixes rather than blame.
concepts.label: Blameless postmortem

concepts.definition: Determining whether a production failure stems from data, model, code, configuration, or infrastructure, or from an adversary.
concepts.label: ML failure attribution

concepts.definition: Treating model, feature, and pipeline configuration as versioned, reviewed, and tested code.
concepts.label: ML configuration management

concepts.definition: Declaring compute, storage, and service infrastructure in versioned machine-readable files from which environments are provisioned.
concepts.label: Infrastructure as code

concepts.definition: Shared internal infrastructure and services that standardize how teams train, deploy, and operate models.
concepts.label: ML platform

concepts.definition: Accumulated system costs from shortcuts in ML code, data dependencies, configuration, and pipelines that make future change slower and riskier.
concepts.label: ML technical debt

concepts.definition: The property that changing any input, feature, or hyperparameter of a model can change its behavior on everything else.
concepts.label: Entanglement

concepts.definition: Systems that use a model's outputs without the model owner's knowledge, creating hidden coupling.
concepts.label: Undeclared consumers

concepts.definition: Staged levels of automation, from manual training and deployment to automated continuous training and delivery.
concepts.label: MLOps maturity

concepts.definition: The division of responsibilities among data, modeling, platform, and operations roles that owns an ML system across its lifecycle.
concepts.label: ML team roles

concepts.definition: Planned withdrawal of a model from service, including notifying and migrating its consumers before removing it.
concepts.label: Model deprecation

concepts.definition: Preserving retired models, data references, and evaluation records needed for audit, reproduction, or rollback after service ends.
concepts.label: Artifact archival

concepts.definition: Policy and mechanisms that set how long data, logs, and derived artifacts are kept and when they are deleted.
concepts.label: Data retention

concepts.definition: Model-required floating-point operations per second achieved, divided by the aggregate peak FLOP rate of the hardware used, excluding recomputation.
concepts.label: Model FLOPs utilization

concepts.definition: Identifying the resource or stage, such as compute, memory bandwidth, I/O, or communication, whose capacity limits end-to-end throughput or latency for a workload.
concepts.label: Bottleneck analysis

concepts.definition: The fraction of allocated accelerator time that produces retained training progress, after losses to scheduling, failures, restarts, and lost work.
concepts.label: Training goodput

concepts.definition: Removing weights, neurons, channels, or other structures judged unimportant from a network, usually followed by fine-tuning to recover quality.
concepts.label: Pruning

concepts.definition: Pruning whole channels, filters, heads, or layers so that the remaining model stays dense and runs faster without sparse-execution support.
concepts.label: Structured pruning

concepts.definition: Approximating a weight matrix or tensor by a product of smaller factors of reduced rank to cut parameters and operations.
concepts.label: Low-rank factorization

concepts.definition: Training or fine-tuning with simulated quantization in the forward pass so the model adapts to reduced precision, in contrast to post-training quantization.
concepts.label: Quantization-aware training

concepts.definition: Automated search over a defined space of network architectures for designs that optimize a stated objective such as accuracy under a cost budget.
concepts.label: Neural architecture search

concepts.definition: Architecture search whose objective includes latency, energy, or memory measured or predicted on the target device rather than proxy counts such as FLOPs.
concepts.label: Hardware-aware NAS

concepts.definition: Factoring a standard convolution into a per-channel spatial convolution followed by a pointwise convolution, reducing operations and parameters.
concepts.label: Depthwise separable convolution

concepts.definition: The set of model configurations for which no alternative improves quality without worsening a stated cost measure, such as latency, memory, or energy, on a stated platform.
concepts.label: Accuracy-efficiency frontier

concepts.definition: Jointly choosing model architecture and hardware or kernel design so that each exploits the other's structure.
concepts.label: Model-hardware co-design

concepts.definition: Reissuing a failed request after increasing, typically jittered, delays and within a retry budget, so that transient faults recover without overloading dependencies.
concepts.label: Retry with backoff

concepts.definition: A client-side guard that stops sending requests to a failing dependency after an error threshold and probes it before resuming traffic.
concepts.label: Circuit breaker

concepts.definition: Maintaining redundant replicas of a service or state and redirecting work to a healthy replica when one fails.
concepts.label: Replication and failover

concepts.definition: Continuing to serve with reduced quality, features, or freshness under failure or overload instead of failing outright.
concepts.label: Graceful degradation

concepts.definition: The checkpoint period that minimizes expected lost time, balancing checkpoint write cost against expected rework, approximately the square root of twice the write cost times MTBF.
concepts.label: Optimal checkpoint interval

concepts.definition: Snapshotting training state quickly to host memory and persisting it in the background so computation resumes before the durable write completes.
concepts.label: Asynchronous checkpointing

concepts.definition: Hardware producing wrong computational results without raising an error or crash, so the corruption propagates undetected.
concepts.label: Silent data corruption

concepts.definition: The expected operating time between failures of a component or system; for independent components, system MTBF shrinks roughly in inverse proportion to component count.
concepts.label: Mean time between failures

concepts.definition: The fraction of time or requests for which a system performs its specified function, approximately MTBF divided by MTBF plus mean time to repair.
concepts.label: Availability

concepts.definition: A partial or degraded failure that some observers detect and others do not, such as a slow or lossy node that still passes health checks.
concepts.label: Gray failure

concepts.definition: A set of components that can fail together from a shared cause, such as a rack, power feed, switch, or software release.
concepts.label: Failure domain

concepts.definition: Detecting or correcting computational errors by carrying checksums through an algorithm, such as matrix multiplication, and verifying invariants on its outputs.
concepts.label: Algorithm-based fault tolerance

concepts.definition: Running controlled experiments that inject real-world failures into production-like systems to test a hypothesis about steady-state behavior.
concepts.label: Chaos engineering

concepts.definition: A scheduled exercise in which teams deliberately trigger failure scenarios to rehearse detection, response, and recovery procedures.
concepts.label: Game day

concepts.definition: Emulating hardware faults such as bit flips in weights, activations, or registers to measure how errors propagate to model outputs.
concepts.label: Hardware fault injection

concepts.definition: The extent of users, components, or effects that a single fault, change, or experiment can impact.
concepts.label: Blast radius

concepts.definition: Implanting a hidden behavior in a model, via poisoned data or modified weights, that activates only on inputs containing an attacker-chosen trigger.
concepts.label: Backdoor attack

concepts.definition: A user-crafted input that induces a model to bypass its safety training or usage policy and produce disallowed output.
concepts.label: Jailbreak

concepts.definition: Training on adversarially perturbed inputs generated during training to increase robustness within a specified perturbation set.
concepts.label: Adversarial training

concepts.definition: Reconstructing a functionally equivalent copy or the parameters of a model by querying its prediction interface.
concepts.label: Model extraction

concepts.definition: Embedding a verifiable signature in a model's parameters or behavior so that ownership of copies or derivatives can later be demonstrated.
concepts.label: Model watermarking

concepts.definition: Cryptographically signing model files and their provenance metadata so that consumers can verify integrity and origin before loading.
concepts.label: Model artifact signing

concepts.definition: Code execution triggered by loading a model stored in an executable serialization format, such as pickle, from an untrusted source.
concepts.label: Unsafe model deserialization

concepts.definition: Introducing malicious or vulnerable components into an ML system through third-party datasets, pretrained weights, libraries, build tools, or hardware.
concepts.label: ML supply-chain compromise

concepts.definition: Inferring whether a specific record was in a model's training data from the model's outputs or parameters.
concepts.label: Membership inference

concepts.definition: Reconstructing sensitive attributes or representative training inputs from a model's outputs, confidence scores, or shared parameter gradients.
concepts.label: Model inversion

concepts.definition: Stochastic gradient descent with per-example gradient clipping and calibrated noise, with privacy loss tracked across steps by an accountant.
concepts.label: DP-SGD

concepts.definition: Removing the influence of specified training records from a trained model, either exactly by retraining or approximately at lower cost.
concepts.label: Machine unlearning

concepts.definition: A cryptographic protocol that lets a server compute the sum of client updates without seeing any individual client's update.
concepts.label: Secure aggregation

concepts.definition: Granting each component or actor only the permissions its task requires, for only as long as it requires them.
concepts.label: Least privilege

concepts.definition: Protecting data and models while in use by running computation inside hardware-isolated, attestable trusted execution environments.
concepts.label: Confidential computing

concepts.definition: A procedure by which a platform proves to a remote verifier the identity and measured state of its hardware and software before receiving secrets.
concepts.label: Remote attestation

concepts.definition: Inferring secrets from observable resource behavior, such as timing, power, memory, or cache contention, across an isolation boundary.
concepts.label: Side-channel attack

concepts.definition: Useful work completed per unit energy, such as inferences or tokens per joule, measured within a stated system boundary.
concepts.label: Energy efficiency

concepts.definition: Greenhouse-gas emissions per unit of electricity supplied, varying by region, time, and generation mix, in grams CO2-equivalent per kilowatt-hour.
concepts.label: Grid carbon intensity

concepts.definition: Emissions from electricity consumed while operating a system, computed from energy use and the carbon intensity of its supply.
concepts.label: Operational carbon

concepts.definition: The GHG Protocol classification of emissions into direct (Scope 1), purchased energy (Scope 2), and value-chain (Scope 3) categories.
concepts.label: Emission scopes

concepts.definition: Shifting flexible workloads in time or location toward periods and regions of lower grid carbon intensity, subject to deadlines and capacity.
concepts.label: Carbon-aware scheduling

concepts.definition: Emissions from manufacturing, transporting, and disposing of hardware and facilities, attributed to a system independent of its operation.
concepts.label: Embodied carbon

concepts.definition: A standardized method for compiling and evaluating a product's environmental inputs, outputs, and impacts from raw materials through disposal.
concepts.label: Life cycle assessment

concepts.definition: Water withdrawn or consumed by a system, on site for cooling and off site for electricity generation, per unit of work or over its lifetime.
concepts.label: Water footprint

concepts.definition: The period a hardware asset stays in service before replacement, over which its embodied impacts and capital cost are amortized.
concepts.label: Hardware service lifetime

concepts.definition: Discarded electronic equipment and components, including retired accelerators and servers, and the hazards and lost materials of their disposal.
concepts.label: Electronic waste
